newsitem.title: USA: U.S. manufacturers' profits rose in Q1.
newsitem.headline: U.S. manufacturers' profits rose in Q1.

text.p: After-tax profits of U.S. manufacturing companies averaged a seasonally adjusted 6.2 cents per dollar of sales in the first quarter of 1997, the Commerce Department said Monday.

That was up from a revised 6.0 cents per dollar of sales in the fourth quarter of 1996 that was previously reported as 6.1 cents. It also was higher than profits a year earlier in the first quarter of 1996, which averaged a seasonally adjusted 5.8 cents per dollar of sales.
Total seasonally adjusted profits after taxes were $59.3 billion on net sales of $964.3 billion in the first quarter.
In the fourth quarter, profits were $57.5 billion on net sales of $959.8 billion. In the first quarter of 1996, profits were $52.9 billion on net sales of $914.9 billion.
The report is based on quarterly financial reports from about 8,300 corporations, the department said.
After-tax profits of non-durable manufacturing companies rose to $31.2 billion in the first quarter from $29.0 billion in the fourth quarter of 1996.
After-tax profits of durables manufacturers fell to $28.1 billion in the first quarter from $28.5 billion in the previous quarter, the department said.
